> V50.3.5 [MODIFIED, MOVED FROM 14.4.7] Verify that the content of the web application cannot be embedded in a third-party site by default, and that embedding of specific resources is allowed only when necessary, using the Content-Security-Policy frame-ancestors directive. > The frame-ancestors directive **obsoletes the X-Frame-Options header**. If a resource has both policies, the frame-ancestors policy SHOULD be enforced and the X-Frame-Options policy SHOULD be ignored.

https://www.w3.org/TR/CSP2/#frame-ancestors-and-frame-options

> The frame-ancestors directive obsoletes the X-Frame-Options header. If a resource has both policies, the frame-ancestors policy SHOULD be enforced and the X-Frame-Options policy SHOULD be ignored.

Excellent point :)

"_V50.3.5 [MODIFIED, MOVED FROM 14.4.7] Verify that the web application uses the frame-ancestors directive of the Content-Security-Policy header field to ensure that it cannot be embedded in a third-party site by default, and that embedding of specific resources is allowed only when necessary. > If a company uses XFO and not the CSP directive, do they fail this requirement?

In practice from an attacker point of view, if I can not do UI redress attack (such as clickjacking), then it does not matter what was used against it.

In practice from a developer point of view, I want to make future-proof solutions and although x-frame-options provides defense in practice today, I don't know when and if it will be deprecated from browsers.

I think with that proposal, do solve one problem you replace it with larger one.

With XFO - we can not say you are safe and we can not say you are not. We may say that _today_ you are ok, but this is not future-proof solution for a requirement. That is why my clear proposal to point it out, that XFO is obsolete.

Rethinking about it - CSP frame-ancestors is must have to use to be sure that you satisfy the requirement.

Additionally, I think we need to remove "in a third-party site", because allowing embedding resources by it's own application (same-origin scope) provides nice bypasses of CSP and other tricks with UI in an HTML injection condition.

> Verify that the web application uses the frame-ancestors directive of the Content-Security-Policy header field to ensure that it cannot be embedded by default and that embedding of specific resources is allowed only when necessary. Note that the X-Frame-Options header field, although supported by browsers, is obsolete.

Note that the proposal has a wider scope than "clickjacking" - as clickjacking is a valid problem only when some clickable UI functionality is exposed to a third party, but the proposed requirement asks to disallow any embedding. As it also covers clickjacking vector we don't need to have a separate one.
